name: Barskoon Syrts (Arabel)
near: Barskoon is the village at the mouth of the gorge, ~50–55 km of road to the plateau (17–20 km to the waterfalls + the pass serpentine); there is no accommodation on the plateau itself. Soyok (OSM, 18.4 km) is the nearest marker, but it is a tract (valley) with no permanent population.
elev: The plateau is 3,700–3,800 m (too.kg: 3,800 m; Destination Jeti Oguz: 3,770 m; Trip to Kyrgyzstan: pass 3,754 m). Higher up the road — the Suyok/Seok Pass 4,016–4,040 m (firsov.kz: 4,016 m; Destination Karakol: 4,022 m; frantsouzov: 4,040 m), the Barskoon Pass 3,816 m (firsov.kz).
short: The Arabel syrts (high plateau) is a tundra plateau at 3,800 m with more than 50 lakes beyond the Barskoon Pass; the only place in the country where you can reach an altitude of 4,000 m in an ordinary car, thanks to the Kumtor mine road.
desc: Beyond the spruce forests and waterfalls of the Barskoon gorge, the Kumtor gravel road climbs in serpentines to the pass (3,754–3,816 m) and comes out onto flat syrts — an ancient glacial floor with glacial basins, bogs and more than fifty lakes (the largest is Arabel), where yaks graze and argali (mountain sheep) are found. The average annual temperature here is below zero (−7…−8 °C per the Trip to Kyrgyzstan catalog), snow lies by the road even in July, and only mosses, lichens and grasses grow. The road continues to the Suyok Pass (4,016–4,040 m) and to the Kumtor mine checkpoint, where tourists are turned back; passage to the plateau and lakes is free after a check of passports and vehicle documents (TripAdvisor, 2024; reports 2018–2021). From the plateau to the west, over the Arabel Pass, the Bolgart valley leads to Naryn, and to the north there are hiking and horse trails to Juuku (Kyrgyz Nomad Trail). There is no infrastructure: no shops, no yurts, no signal — only a tent and the wind.
guide: This is the fastest “four-thousander” in Kyrgyzstan: from warm Barskoon you are at 3,800 m in an hour, which makes it more dangerous than it seems — a headache and shortness of breath hit suddenly, so drink water and don’t run. Take your passport and vehicle documents: they are checked at the checkpoint, and you won’t be let past the lakes and the Suyok Pass (4,022 m) — that is the mine. The best shots are in the morning at Lake Arabel, when the water is like a mirror and the snowfields are reflected; by lunchtime the wind rises. If you spend the night in a tent, count on frost and on the nearest person being 30 km away. Boil river water — the mine is upstream. You will see yaks and, with luck, argali.
see: The serpentine up to the Barskoon Pass with a view of Issyk-Kul; Lake Arabel and dozens of small lakes; snowfields by the road and the glaciers of Terskey (Petrov Glacier ~4,300 m — not accessible); yaks, argali, marmots; the Suyok Pass (4,022 m) — the highest point of the road; the Gagarin monument and the waterfalls in the gorge on the way.
skip: You have heart/blood pressure problems or children under 5 — a sharp gain to 3,800 m. The weather is overcast: without sun the plateau is gray tundra. You are already planning Song-Kol or Kel-Suu — the impression of the syrts will be similar.
diff: By car — easy (gravel road, a passenger car gets through — TripAdvisor 2024, firsov.kz 2019); physiologically — an altitude of 3,800–4,000 m without acclimatization. Hiking/bike/horse routes via Juuku are hard, multi-day and self-sufficient.
when: June–September (lakes ice-free, the road dry); July–August — yaks on the jailoo (summer pasture); in May and October — snow on the plateau is possible on any day. The road is cleared year-round (Kumtor), in winter — ski touring (TripAdvisor), but −20 °C and below.
hours: Open terrain, 24 hours. The Kumtor checkpoint on the road checks documents in daylight; beyond the checkpoint (the mine) — closed to everyone. No fee (TripAdvisor, 2024).
daytime: Morning (8–11 am): calm, mirror-like lakes, clear sky; after 1–2 pm — wind, clouds, thunderstorms/snow. Overnight stays — only for the prepared.
how: From Barskoon along the Kumtor gravel road up the gorge: 17–20 km to the waterfall area, then the serpentine to the Barskoon Pass (3,754–3,816 m) and out onto the plateau — about 1–2 h from the village in all (TripAdvisor 2024; frantsouzov: to 3,800 m about an hour). From Karakol — 80–90 km to Barskoon + the plateau, a day round trip. An alternative is on foot/on horseback/by bike from the Juuku gorge (too.kg).
needcar: Yes, essential: there is no public transport, and it is 50+ km and 2,000 m of gain from the village. A passenger car is suitable (gravel road); for turning off to the lakes — an SUV.
self: Yes, by car: the road is unambiguous; carry your passport and vehicle documents for the checkpoint; no border-zone permit is needed (it is not a border zone). Self-sufficiency: food, water, fuel, warm clothing.
roadtype: The Kumtor gravel industrial road: “an excellent dirt road, packed down by trucks”, passable for a sedan and a motorcycle (firsov.kz 2019, pikabu 2021, TripAdvisor 2024 — “very good in summer 2024”); a serpentine with steep climbs; turn-offs to the lakes — soft ground, ruts, easy to get stuck (frantsouzov 2018).
traveltime: Barskoon – plateau: 1–2 h (TripAdvisor 2024); Karakol – plateau – Karakol: 7–9 h of pure driving (Destination Karakol). On foot from Barskoon — more than 30 km (frantsouzov).
stay: On the plateau — only a tent (too.kg: no shops, cafés or guesthouses; many places for camping). The nearest accommodation is the guesthouses of Barskoon and Tamga, and yurt cafés at the waterfalls (seasonal, an overnight stay is not guaranteed). Prices are not published.
net: No signal (too.kg; Destination Karakol: “no cellular signal”). The last signal is in Barskoon village/the lower part of the gorge. A satellite messenger for self-sufficient routes.
entry: Free; at the checkpoint only a document check (TripAdvisor, 2024). There are no paid services on the plateau.
transfer: A jeep tour from Karakol €210–250 per car (Destination Karakol, 2025–2026); a transfer Karakol – Barskoon 9,900 som (MYWAY, 2026); a taxi from the village to the plateau — not published.
bring: Passport and vehicle documents; a warm jacket, hat, gloves (+5 °C and snow in summer); sun protection (UV at 3,800 m); water 2 L/person and a snack; altitude-sickness pills on a doctor’s advice (Destination Karakol recommends Diamox if you do not adapt); a full tank; an offline map; for a night out — a winter sleeping bag and a tent.
warn: A sharp gain to 3,800–4,000 m in an hour — a risk of altitude sickness; with a headache and nausea, descend. The Kumtor mine territory is closed, and the checkpoint checks documents; do not leave the road near the industrial zone. No signal, accommodation or fuel; the weather changes within minutes, snow in any month. River water — boil (the mine is upstream). Kumtor trucks on the serpentine — give way.
food: There is no food on the plateau — bring your own. On the way: yurt cafés at the Barskoon waterfalls (shashlik, lagman, kumis, seasonal), ashkans (eateries) in Barskoon and Tamga. A lunch box on the tour — 600 som (Destination Karakol).
reviews: Google Maps “Arabel Plateau”: 5.0/5, 24 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Barskoon Plateau”: 4.8/5, 8 reviews (the latest — July 2024). Pros: accessibility in an ordinary car, lakes, yaks, “Martian” views; cons: cold and wind, being turned back at the checkpoint, no infrastructure.
p.sum: The plateau at 3,800 m is reachable in 1–2 h from the village of Barskoon along the Kumtor mine gravel road — in summer even a sedan gets through, but turn-offs to the lakes are better in a 4×4. Be sure to have your passport and vehicle documents (a document-check checkpoint), a full tank, food, water and warm clothing: on the plateau there is no accommodation, signal or café. Without your own car — a Destination Karakol jeep tour (€210–250 per car, 7–9 h) or a taxi from Barskoon/Tamga by arrangement. Stay overnight in Tamga/Barskoon; a tent on the plateau is only for the prepared (frost and snow even in July).

p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: the Barskoon waterfalls, a night in Tamga. Day 2: dawn and morning at Arabel (calm), descent, Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Tosor beach.
p.iti.2.title: Expedition
p.iti.2.plan: Barskoon → Arabel → Juuku Pass → Juukuchak hot springs → Saruu (2–4 days on foot/on horseback) or Arabel → Bolgart → Naryn (bike/4×4).
p.season: June — snow by the road, the lakes may be frozen; July–August — the best time, yaks on the pastures, but hail and snow are possible; September — clear and cold, the first snowfalls; October–May — the road is cleared, but −20 °C and below, only with a guide.
p.budget.economy: Hitchhiking/a taxi from Barskoon by arrangement (split among a group); your own food; a tent or a guesthouse in Tamga ~1,500–2,000/person. ≈ 3,000–5,000 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Destination Karakol jeep tour €210–250 per car (÷3–5 ≈ 4,500–7,000 som) + lunch box 600 + a hotel in Karakol. ≈ 8,000–12,000 som/person.
p.permits: No border-zone permit is needed. On the road there is a document-check checkpoint: passport + vehicle registration/power of attorney; beyond the Suyok Pass is the Kumtor mine, where tourists are turned back. No fee (2024).
p.access: Not recommended with children under 5 and for people with heart/lung diseases (a rapid gain to 3,800–4,000 m). For older people — only by car, with no exertion, for a short time. Stroller — no. For dogs — cold and altitude.
